userDirection: Preserve centre section and sticker. Replace top and bottom strips with new natural vegetable arrangements in photorealistic style. Interior illustration style is explicitly waived for this exercise.
prompt:
Create ONE complete flat front book cover by editing reference 1. The user wants a radically different PHOTOGRAPHIC experiment for the two image strips ONLY. Reference 1 is a layout, lettering and sticker reference, NOT a vegetable-art style reference.

LOCK THE CENTRAL DESIGN: faithfully preserve the existing cream central section, its exact proportions and colour, the dark green lettering and every word, spacing, line break and size. Preserve the little illustrated two-leaf title sprout as a graphic logo. Exact words: 'The' / 'Vegetable' / 'Guru'; 'Your at-a-glance' / 'growing companion'; 'John Lennon'. Preserve the white circular YouTube sticker exactly as it is: same lower-right position and diameter, same shallow shadow, same gentle 5-degree clockwise tilt, same red play mark and exact words 'As seen on' / 'YouTube' / '@hackriculture'. It remains visibly ON TOP of the photographic imagery and slightly overlaps the cream centre. Do not retype, redesign, move or enlarge anything in the centre or sticker.

REPLACE BOTH ILLUSTRATED STRIPS COMPLETELY with convincing photorealistic editorial food still-life photography of real freshly harvested UK garden vegetables. Do not merely put photographic textures on the old cartoon silhouettes. Create NEW natural arrangements, photographed overhead on the same continuous, subdued very dark forest-green painted potting-table surface, faint honest surface texture, not rustic brown wood. Soft broad natural window/daylight from upper left, restrained natural saturation, real delicate skin texture, leaf veins, papery onion skin, faint earth traces and believable diffuse contact shadows. Sharp enough to see the produce clearly. The two strips are different crops of one coherent photographic session, not a tiled collage or floating isolated cutouts.

TOP STRIP: keep its existing exact band height, approximately the top 23% of the cover. A casual freshly picked handful of small and medium tomatoes at the left, some gently touching and partly overlapping, one attached to a short real tomato vine with a few serrated tomato leaflets; a modest red onion and a naturally resting half onion around the centre-right, some loose papery skin; a few pea pods and one opened pod toward the right, not oversized, with naturally unequal peas and delicate pea tendrils. Arrange them as a gardener might set down a harvest on a work surface, with believable gravity, relaxed oblique orientations, uneven gaps and some objects partly cropped by the outer cover edge. No evenly spaced specimen row, no giant upright onion like a display trophy, no identical shiny tomatoes or waxy leaves. These are REAL vegetables lying on a REAL surface. Leave a little dark-green space between loosely connected groups. No generic decorative foliage unrelated to the crops.

BOTTOM STRIP: keep its existing exact band height, approximately the bottom 31% of the cover. A small loose harvest of 4 or 5 authentic carrots left of centre, all different lengths and girths, slight natural bends, tiny roots and sparse dry soil specks. Most lie loosely together as they were picked up, with a couple angled away or partly tucked underneath and one naturally overlapping a neighbour. Their roots and finely divided feathery carrot tops settle on the surface, with coherent contact shadows. NOT a neatly crossed X, radial star, symmetric fan, stacked orange chevrons or isolated objects 'plonked' on a background. Show a naturally observed pile, not a diagram. A few fine carrot fronds may cross slightly into the cream at far left, clear of all words, replacing the illustrated fronds. A small relaxed bundle of genuine curly purple-stemmed kale leaves lies to the right, partly behind the sticker; include believable folds, different leaf faces and real branching veins. A subtle cropped edge or stray frond can suggest the harvest continues beyond the frame. Enough quiet dark-green surface remains to avoid cramming.

All vegetables, foliage, light and shadows in the strips must look like high-quality genuine camera photography, absolutely no vector illustration, brushwork, painted modelling, plastic CGI surfaces, artificial rim lighting or cartoon foliage. No human hands, tools, crates, new words or added labels. Keep the central lettering/logo and sticker GRAPHIC exactly as in the reference. One clean full portrait cover, same 185:240 proportions, no spine, no mockup, no background outside the cover.
back: Revision 07 native back retained; John says it looks much better. No further back changes requested.
